steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Why Soliloquies Matter: They give direct access to a character's psychology. In "Macbeth," soliloquies show his internal conflict, ambition, guilt, and eventual nihilism. | Track language changes: How a character speaks at the beginning vs the end shows their development (or deterioration). | Shakespeare Language Strategy: Focus on three layers: verse form (iambic pentameter, blank verse, prose), imagery patterns (blood, darkness, clothing), and rhetorical devices (repetition, antithesis, soliloquy). When the rhythm breaks, something significant is happening — always ask why. Track how a character's language changes across the play as evidence of development.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: What is iambic pentameter and why does Shakespeare use it? | What's the difference between a soliloquy and an aside? | What does the blood imagery represent in "Macbeth"?
